description: This PHP source file defines the LogRecordIterator class within the Aws\CloudTrail namespace. The class provides an iterator interface to traverse AWS CloudTrail log records stored in S3 buckets, supporting multiple ways to instantiate such iterators (for entire trails, specific buckets, or individual files). It interacts with S3 and CloudTrail clients, reads log files, and yields individual log records as associative arrays.

classes.name: LogRecordIterator
classes.description: Iterator class providing access to AWS CloudTrail log records stored in S3, supporting iteration over log files and log records.

methods.name: forTrail
methods.description: Static factory method to create an iterator for a trail using S3 and CloudTrail clients with options.

methods.name: forBucket
methods.description: Static factory method to create an iterator for all log files in a specified S3 bucket.

methods.name: forFile
methods.description: Static factory method to create an iterator for a specific log file given its bucket and object key.

methods.name: __construct
methods.description: Constructor initializing the iterator with a LogFileReader and a log file iterator.

methods.name: current
methods.description: Returns the current log record as an array, or false if the iterator is invalid.

methods.name: next
methods.description: Advances the iterator to the next log record, loading new records from the next log file when necessary.

methods.name: key
methods.description: Returns a unique key for the current log record, typically combining the file key and record index.

methods.name: valid
methods.description: Checks if the current position in the iterator points to a valid log record.

methods.name: rewind
methods.description: Resets the iterator to the start, loading initial records from the first log file.

methods.name: getInnerIterator
methods.description: Returns the underlying log file iterator.

methods.name: loadRecordsFromCurrentLogFile
methods.description: Reads and loads log records from the current log file in the logFileIterator.
